data.name: Captivity
data.detailed_description:
You wake up to the smell of rotting flesh in what can only be described as someone's basement. Your memory is blank and your vision impaired, you have no idea where you are. The floors and walls are dirty, it appears there may be other people here as there are dirty sheets on the floor. There is shouting coming from above but there seems to be no other way out than up the stairs.

Captivity is a new bloody horror experience featuring death, hopelessness and a tense atmosphere, it is up to you to escape captivity and deal with what ever stands in your way.

reviews.review:
Step right up ladies and gentlemen to another spectacularly awful buck 'o nine horror game. Today's crapfest is brought to us by newcomer dev Trauma, and second-time publisher New Worlds Games. Do you like long loading times? Do you enjoy enemies that defy the boundaries of the game? Do you like dying in one hit? Well step on up, because Captivity has all of that, and much more!

This is not your standard Unity Personal Edition horror game, so luckily this title has good optimization as far as FPS goes. However, it's made in FPS Creator, so there are long load times, glitches, and random crashing instead. During my 24 minutes with the game, it crashed twice, and upon the last crash I just gave up entirely. It's not that the premise of Captivity is bad, and in fact the atmosphere within it is quite good; there's tons of blood, body parts, and tense music to satisfy a B-Grade gore craving. What's wrong with the game is everything else.

It's your basic key finding simulator with fighting mechanics thrown in; bad ones, I might add. As far as I know, from making it to the 5th level, the only enemy types are ICP inspired Juggalos (I wish I was joking) who wield machetes... until the end of the 5th level where they somehow get guns. That's an excellent idea, let's give the horrible enemy AI guns when you die in one hit. Granted, the level also gives you a gun, but no HUD that explains that you do in fact have a limited number of bullets. I unfortunately saved right after expending my last bullet, leaving me to load a save where I was continually getting headshot by some clown before I could even move.

If that isn't bad enough, your hitbox is enormous. I mean you are FAT. Either that or the ICP Juggalos activate their Go-Go-Gadget arms to reach you. Facing them one on one is hard enough when you die in one hit, but get this... they clip through the walls. Yes! The first time you encounter them, there are three of them behind a door with a fence. These mofos came straight through the wall. I died at this part the first time without knowing what was going on, and when I reloaded I saw machetes sticking through the plaster, moving; they kept moving until they finally clipped through. This happens on every level, so you'll die out of nowhere until you learn to look for the spawns and find out where they're clipping through at.

Crashing? Check. Huge hitbox? Check. One enemy type? Check. Unfair gameplay that goes beyond "it's just a hard game"? Check. I might also mention that each time you load a save there might be something different that wasn't there before, such as an out of place Juggalo. Also, you do get a chainsaw at some point but it's SO loud you'll never want to use it... RIP ears. To sum it up, Captivity has a decent atmosphere and a relatively good idea story-wise, but its execution is horrid.

[h1]Rating: [b]1.0/5.0[/b] - It's Bad.[/h1]
